title: Intensified Russian Strikes Are "Tearing Kyiv Apart," Mayor Warns
summary:
The mayor of Kyiv has warned that intensified Russian drone and missile strikes are "tearing Kyiv apart." Vitaliy Klitschko said the Ukrainian capital is in a "very dramatic situation" as Russia hits its critical infrastructure, logistics, housing and other key facilities. He spoke after Kyiv's defence council held a crisis meeting.

The latest attacks focused on the Pivdennyi (Southern) bridge, one of the main transport arteries across the Dnipro River, which divides western and eastern Kyiv. A Russian drone hit the bridge overnight, and on Friday evening it was struck again, the fourth time in two days. All metro and automobile traffic is now suspended across the bridge, causing major delays, and restrictions are in place on Kyiv's two other key bridges. The city has an estimated population of about three million, and many residents rely heavily on the metro network. Kyiv's data centers have also been hit recently, causing internet outages. Ukraine's state emergencies service said one person was killed when a multi-storey residential building was hit overnight.

Klitschko said Russia's aim is to "sow panic," but he said the capital would prevail through the joint efforts of those who love it and care for it.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russian President Vladimir Putin decided in early September that "there are no rules now" when attacking Ukraine. In an excerpt from an interview with the Financial Times, Zelensky said Russia has failed to occupy Ukraine, so it is now carrying out massive attacks, and that Russians "want people to flee their cities."

Putin insisted that Russia's attacks on Ukrainian economic targets are a direct response to Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil refineries and ships in the Black Sea. "Now from every direction we're receiving calls 'let's stop'. But they started it," Putin said. The BBC notes that Russia was the first to launch attacks on energy facilities, and that it has ramped up attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure every winter since the full-scale invasion in 2022.
why_it_matters: Repeated strikes on bridges, data centers and housing show how war can disrupt daily life for millions of people far from the front line.

questions.question: What did Mayor Klitschko call the situation in Kyiv?
options: A "quiet week"
A "temporary problem"
A "normal winter delay"
A "very dramatic situation"

questions.question: What happened to the Pivdennyi bridge on Friday evening?
options: It was struck again, the fourth time in two days
It was closed for a planned safety inspection by city workers
It was struck for the very first time that week
It was repaired and fully reopened to all traffic again
questions.correct_answer: It was struck again, the fourth time in two days

questions.question: According to Klitschko, what is Russia's aim?
options: To close all schools
To help rebuild roads
To end the war quickly
To sow panic

questions.question: What did Zelensky say Putin decided in early September?
options: That the war should stop
That "there are no rules now"
That trade should resume
That bridges would be rebuilt

questions.question: How does Putin explain Russia's attacks on Ukrainian economic targets?
options: As a reaction to the mayor's crisis meeting in the capital
As a reply to a Financial Times interview with Zelensky
As a response to Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil refineries and Black Sea ships
As a plan to protect Kyiv's bridges from a flood
questions.correct_answer: As a response to Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil refineries and Black Sea ships

Only winter storms have damaged the energy sites
Ukraine was first to launch such attacks on energy facilities
